policy: References informed shell proportions (spire angle, whorl count, body-whorl fraction, aperture shape, sculpture type), soft-part layout (siphon length, foot outline, metapodial tails, tentacle and eye placement) and colour placement only. No pixels were sampled, traced, copied or redistributed. Seller imagery was not used as a texture or tracing source; public seller descriptions guided trade identity only.
taxonomyNote: The trade name Nassarius snail (user spelling 'Nasseria') covers several nassariid species sold as sand-sifting cleanup crew (Nassarius vibex, now Phrontis vibex, N. distortus, N. coronatus and others). The asset is authored at genus/group level as Nassarius sp. with taxonomyConfidence 'genus'; SeaLifeBase size data for Phrontis vibex (the most common trade species) anchors the scale.

referenceGradeRationale: Shell proportions and sculpture are well documented for the genus and openly licensed shell photographs in apertural and dorsal views are available; the soft-part pose (siphon carriage, foot spread while crawling) is inferred from descriptive accounts and general nassariid behaviour rather than calibrated side/top/front photographs of a crawling animal, and the trade group spans several species.
